title: Reserve Terms Across the Keyturn Host Payout Schedules
content:
Money a host has earned may be held back on a Keyturn Host Payout Account rather than paid out. What share is held, how long it is held for and what frees it are terms of the schedule the account settles under.

## Terms by schedule

| Payout schedule | Routine reserve share | Routine hold period | Routine release trigger | New-host reserve share | Trips ending the new-host reserve | Claim reserve multiple | Claim reserve ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | 0 percent | 0 days | When the trip settles | 20 percent | 5 | 1 | 5000.00 USD |
| Weekly Batch | 0 percent | 0 days | When the trip settles | 15 percent | 5 | 1 | 7500.00 USD |
| Express | 5 percent | 7 days | When the hold days have run | 10 percent | 10 | 1.25 | 10000.00 USD |
| Instant | 10 percent | 7 days | When the hold days have run | 10 percent | 10 | 1.5 | 15000.00 USD |
| Fleet Settlement | 3 percent | 30 days | When the claim closes | 0 percent | 0 | 1 | 50000.00 USD |
| Reserve-Backed Settlement | 15 percent | 60 days | When the claim closes | 0 percent | 0 | 2 | 100000.00 USD |

## Terms answered

**What share of an earning is held as routine reserve?** The routine reserve share of the schedule, from nothing at all on the Keyturn Standard Payout Schedule and the Keyturn Weekly Batch Payout Schedule up to 15 percent on the Keyturn Reserve-Backed Settlement Schedule.

**For how long, and what frees it?** For the routine hold period in calendar days, and it is freed on the trigger the schedule names: when the trip settles, when the hold days have run, or when the claim closes.

**What is held from a host still in their first trips?** The new-host reserve share, which stands at 20 percent on the Keyturn Standard Payout Schedule and falls to nothing on the Keyturn Fleet Settlement Schedule and the Keyturn Reserve-Backed Settlement Schedule; the trips column gives the number of settled trips after which it stops being taken.

**How much is held against an open claim?** The claimed amount taken at the schedule's claim reserve multiple, subject to the schedule's claim reserve ceiling. On the Keyturn Instant Payout Schedule a hypothetical claim of 4000.00 USD gives 6000.00 USD at the multiple of 1.5, which is below that schedule's ceiling of 15000.00 USD and so stands in full; a hypothetical claim of 20000.00 USD gives 30000.00 USD at the same multiple, which is above that ceiling and so is held at 15000.00 USD.
